classification.difficultyReason: Convert units, identify half of a symmetric triangle and interpret a rounded practical result.

content.prompt: A soccer pitch is 100 m from goal to goal. A piece of rope of length 100 metres is attached to the base of each opposing goal. The rope’s length is increased by (only) 20 centimetres. The rope is now loose and can be picked up in the middle to form a triangle. Find the height of the triangle in metres, accurate to two decimal places. Can a mouse fit under the rope?

spec.description: Horizontal ground between two opposing goals, with rope endpoints at their bases and a raised apex above the midpoint. Decorative net detail and ground shading are omitted.
spec.mathematics: A symmetric rope triangle spans the 100 m base; the diagram is schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: No height or calculated rope lengths are supplied.

answer.short: $3.16\text{ m}$. Yes, a mouse can fit beneath the raised middle of the rope.
answer.worked:
The increased rope length is $100+0.20=100.20\text{ m}$. Each half is $50.10\text{ m}$ and half the pitch length is $50\text{ m}$.
Let $h$ metres be the height.
$$\begin{align*}h^2+50^2&=50.10^2\\h^2&=2510.01-2500\\h^2&=10.01\\h&=\sqrt{10.01}\\h&\approx3.16\end{align*}$$
The height is $3.16\text{ m}$ to two decimal places, so a mouse can fit beneath the raised middle.
